chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaina, from Ibn Bukayr and others, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:

Indeed, the divorce which God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded in His Book, and which the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) established as Sunnah, is that the man should separate from the wife. Then when she menstruates and becomes pure from her menstruation, he should call two just men as witnesses to a divorce pronouncement while she is pure and without sexual intercourse. And he is more entitled to take her back (rij'ah) as long as three quru' have not elapsed. And every divorce apart from this is invalid — it is not a divorce.

key_terms.رجعة: Rij'ah — the husband's right to revoke a pronouncement of divorce and resume the marriage without a new contract, during the waiting period
key_terms.طلاق السنة: Divorce according to the Sunnah — the valid form of divorce prescribed by the Prophet
key_terms.عِدَّة: Iddah — the mandatory waiting period after divorce before remarriage
key_terms.قُرُوء: Quru' — the waiting period measured by menstrual cycles or purity periods (scholarly difference of opinion: Shia tradition generally counts complete purity periods)

ai.seo_question: What conditions are required for a valid divorce (talaq) in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) defines the legally valid form of divorce (talaq al-sunnah) as prescribed both by the Quran and the prophetic practice. The hadith specifies three essential conditions: (1) the wife must be in a state of ritual purity (tahara) during which no intercourse has occurred; (2) two just witnesses must be present; and (3) the husband retains the right of revocation (rij'ah) until three complete menstrual cycles elapse. Any divorce not meeting these conditions is declared null and void. This teaching was particularly important for early Muslim communities who encountered pre-Islamic divorce customs and needed clear guidance on valid Islamic divorce procedure.
